verdict.rationale: Sill mainly streams an existing Mac window or the whole desktop to the iPhone or iPad, which is remote viewing rather than an extended display. Its optional virtual display does move a streamed window onto a separate display on the Mac, so the device effectively shows its own display space. That feature is single-window, off by default, and described as keeping the window updating rather than as extending the desktop. Missing for 10: documented use of the device as a full extended desktop display (arrangement, resolution, dragging windows across), and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, a tablet or spare device works as an additional display that extends the desktop, not only a mirror of it

citations.quote: The virtual display (off by default) moves a window you stream onto a display of its own on your Mac, so it keeps updating when other windows cover it.
Sill shows a window from your Mac, or its whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad
